card.title: 121st INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.text: Destruction: Add an OUTRAGE to your hand.
card.flavorText: The 121st Infantry Regiment was a unit of the 30th Infantry Division of the US Army during WWII. When America entered the war in 1941 the division spent two years training in the US before being shipped to France where it landed at Omaha Beach five days after the D-Day landings. There the division participated in Operation Cobra, which was a successful attempt to break out of the Normandy beachhead and end the stalemate. That summer the division continued fighting in France, but after the liberation of Paris it advanced into Belgium and the Netherlands. The division later fought in the Battle of Hürtgen Forest and the Battle of the Bulge, facing fierce resistance from German forces in challenging terrain and harsh winter conditions. After crossing the Rhine the division helped to mop up enemy pockets of resistance. While capturing the city of Braunschweig the division freed 2,500 prisoners from Weferlingen, which was a camp of Buchenwald. The division then met up with the Soviet Red Army at Grunewald on the Elbe River in April 1945, and soon after the war was over.
